long_biography.plain_text:
Kompass Kapital emerged in 2014 as a formal home for operating interests that began in healthcare staffing and technology. It now allocates capital through direct and passive investments, with holdings spanning private aviation, broadband infrastructure, residential services, freight logistics and managed IT. Jayson Alexander Kuti serves as a co-founding partner, helping steward the Kansas City investment platform rather than running every business it backs.

One holding is more directly attributable to Kuti. He owns at least three quarters of the shares and voting rights in Britain's LightSpeed Fibre Holdings and can appoint or remove directors. That documented control does not resolve how his principal capital was formed. The businesses preceding Kompass arose before his known leadership, and their creation is not assigned to him. Whether his wealth came from his own ventures, inheritance, another family transfer or some combination remains unclear. Firm assets and portfolio-company property are not his personal net worth.
